fullPassage: [P01] In a recent study, participants included both males and females ranging in age from 12 to 83. During the experiment, they were given a variety of breakfasts, and sometimes they had to skip breakfast completely. Special tests, including blood tests and endurance tests, were set up to analyze how well their bodies functioned when they had eaten a certain kind of breakfast. The results showed that if people eat an adequate breakfast, they will work more efficiently and more productively than if they skip breakfast or eat a very poor breakfast. This fact appears to be especially true if a person’s work involves mental activity. The study showed that if schoolchildren eat fruit, eggs, bread, and milk before going to school, they will learn more quickly and will be able to concentrate on their lessons for a longer period of time than if their breakfast diet is inadequate. [P02] In one fascinating study, the psychologists Stephanie Clancy and Stephen Dollinger recruited 201 college students and instructed them to collect 12 photographs that “describe who you are as you see yourself.” The students themselves could take the photographs, they could ask other people to take the photographs, or they could use photographs that had already been taken. Clancy and Dollinger found that male students were more likely to submit pictures that captured them engaged in an activity (such as playing a sport), displaying prized possessions (such as a car), or alone. Female students were more likely to submit pictures of themselves with other people. The authors concluded that women tend to define themselves more in terms of their relationships while men tend to define themselves more in terms of their abilities and accomplishments—terms reflective of their individuality, independence, and separateness. [C01] Habits provide a way to reduce the amount of mental energy that must be expended on routine tasks. Habits also form a mindset, which gives us cues on how to behave in certain settings. So when we enter a familiar setting, like the streets around our house, habitual behavior takes over. On the one hand, this is efficient: It frees us from having to gather all sorts of new information, from getting sidetracked. Yet on the other hand, because we are expending less energy on analyzing what is around us, we may be letting our mental guard down. If in three years there has never been a car coming out of the neighborhood’s driveway in the morning, what happens on the first day of the fourth year, when suddenly there is? Will we see it in time? Will we see it at all? Our feeling of safety and control is also a weakness. A study by a group of Israeli researchers found that drivers committed more traffic violations on familiar routes than on unfamiliar routes. [C02] People know knowledge is power and hence make their peers dependent on them. Sometimes people do not ask others for their knowledge as they feel guilty and they try to acquire the same by themselves. Some people do not know that whatever they know will be very useful for others for innovation and accomplishing tasks. People think that if they share knowledge with others, besides getting no recognition or acknowledgment from the beneficiaries, they may be blamed for no reason if application of their knowledge fails or does not provide good results. Also, people do not get time to talk to others. Each one is busy and pressurized by deadlines, milestones and targets. Functional silos, wrong methods of acquiring knowledge, lack of knowledge about technology, too much emphasis on information systems, competitive spirit, decision making process and individual attitudes, and values are some of the barriers of knowledge sharing.

❌ ① habitual(습관적인)은 익숙한 환경에서 습관적 행동이 지배한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② sidetracked(옆길로 빠지는)는 새 정보를 모으거나 옆길로 빠지지 않게 해준다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ safety(안전)는 안전감과 통제감이 약점이기도 하다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ avoided(피했다)는 committed(저질렀다)의 반의어로, 운전자가 익숙한 경로에서 교통 위반을 '피했다'는 뜻이 되어 원문과 반대 ←정답
det.tip: commit violations(위반을 저지르다) ↔ avoid violations(위반을 피하다). 익숙한 경로에서 오히려 위반이 많다는 역설.

questions.passage: [P01] In a recent study, participants included both males and females ranging in age from 12 to 83. During the experiment, they were given a variety of breakfasts, and sometimes they had to skip breakfast completely. Special tests, including blood tests and __________ tests, were set up to analyze how well their bodies functioned when they had eaten a certain kind of breakfast. The results showed that if people eat an adequate breakfast, they will work more efficiently and more productively than if they skip breakfast or eat a very poor breakfast. This fact appears to be especially true if a person’s work involves mental activity. The study showed that if schoolchildren eat fruit, eggs, bread, and milk before going to school, they will learn more quickly and will be able to concentrate on their lessons for a longer period of time than if their breakfast diet is inadequate. [P02] In one fascinating study, the psychologists Stephanie Clancy and Stephen Dollinger recruited 201 college students and instructed them to collect 12 photographs that “describe who you are as you see yourself.” The students themselves could take the photographs, they could ask other people to take the photographs, or they could use photographs that had already been taken. Clancy and Dollinger found that male students were more likely to submit pictures that captured them engaged in an activity (such as playing a sport), displaying prized possessions (such as a car), or alone. Female students were more likely to submit pictures of themselves with other people. The authors concluded that women tend to define themselves more in terms of their relationships while men tend to define themselves more in terms of their abilities and accomplishments—terms reflective of their individuality, independence, and separateness. [C01] Habits provide a way to reduce the amount of mental energy that must be expended on routine tasks. Habits also form a mindset, which gives us cues on how to behave in certain settings. So when we enter a familiar setting, like the streets around our house, habitual behavior takes over. On the one hand, this is efficient: It frees us from having to gather all sorts of new information, from getting sidetracked. Yet on the other hand, because we are expending less energy on analyzing what is around us, we may be letting our mental guard down. If in three years there has never been a car coming out of the neighborhood’s driveway in the morning, what happens on the first day of the fourth year, when suddenly there is? Will we see it in time? Will we see it at all? Our feeling of safety and control is also a weakness. A study by a group of Israeli researchers found that drivers committed more traffic violations on familiar routes than on unfamiliar routes. [C02] People know knowledge is power and hence make their peers dependent on them. Sometimes people do not ask others for their knowledge as they feel guilty and they try to acquire the same by themselves. Some people do not know that whatever they know will be very useful for others for innovation and accomplishing tasks. People think that if they share knowledge with others, besides getting no recognition or acknowledgment from the beneficiaries, they may be blamed for no reason if application of their knowledge fails or does not provide good results. Also, people do not get time to talk to others. Each one is busy and pressurized by deadlines, milestones and targets. Functional silos, wrong methods of acquiring knowledge, lack of knowledge about technology, too much emphasis on information systems, competitive spirit, decision making process and individual attitudes, and values are some of the barriers of knowledge sharing.

det.korean: 남성은 자신의 능력과 성취로 자신을 정의하는 경향이 있다 — 이는 그들의 개별성, 독립성, 분리성을 반영하는 용어이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① collectivism(집단주의)은 남성이 독립적으로 자신을 정의한다는 맥락의 반대 개념이다
❌ ② dependency(의존성)는 남성이 능력과 성취로 자신을 정의한다는 문맥의 반대이다
✅ ③ individuality(개별성)는 남성의 능력/성취 중심 자기정의가 개별성, 독립성, 분리성을 반영한다는 원문에 정확히 맞는다 ←정답
❌ ④ conformity(순응)는 독립성과 분리성이라는 맥락에 맞지 않는다

det.korean: 어떤 사람들은 자신이 아는 것이 다른 사람들의 혁신과 과업 수행에 매우 유용할 것이라는 것을 모른다.
det.analysis:

❌ ③ destruction(파괴)은 '파괴와 과업 수행'이라는 표현이 부자연스럽다
❌ ④ isolation(고립)은 '고립과 과업 수행'이라는 표현이 문맥에 맞지 않는다

det.korean: recruited = 모집하다, 참여시키다

❌ ② dismissed(해산시키다)는 모집의 반대 개념이다
❌ ③ rejected(거부하다)는 참여시키는 것과 반대이다
❌ ④ excluded(배제하다)는 모집과 반대되는 의미이다

det.korean: beneficiaries = 수혜자, 혜택을 받는 사람
det.analysis:
❌ ① competitors(경쟁자)는 혜택을 받는 사람이 아닌 경쟁하는 사람이다
❌ ② opponents(반대자)는 전혀 다른 의미이다
✅ ③ recipients(수령자)는 beneficiaries(수혜자)와 동의어로, 지식을 받는 사람이라는 의미이다 ←정답
❌ ④ donors(기부자)는 주는 사람으로, 받는 사람의 반대이다
det.tip: beneficiary = benefit(혜택) + -ary(~하는 사람) = 수혜자. recipient = receive(받다)의 명사형 = 수령자.

Yet on the other hand, because we are expending less energy on analyzing what is around us, we may be letting our mental guard down. If in three years there has never been a car coming out of the neighborhood’s driveway in the morning, what happens on the first day of the fourth year, when suddenly there is? Will we see it in time? Will we see it at all? Our feeling of safety and control is also a weakness. A study by a group of Israeli researchers found that drivers committed more traffic violations on familiar routes than on unfamiliar routes. [C02] People know knowledge is power and hence make their peers dependent on them. Sometimes people do not ask others for their knowledge as they feel guilty and they try to acquire the same by themselves. Some people do not know that whatever they know will be very useful for others for innovation and accomplishing tasks. People think that if they share knowledge with others, besides getting no recognition or acknowledgment from the beneficiaries, they may be blamed for no reason if application of their knowledge fails or does not provide good results. Also, people do not get time to talk to others. Each one is busy and pressurized by deadlines, milestones and targets. Functional silos, wrong methods of acquiring knowledge, lack of knowledge about technology, too much emphasis on information systems, competitive spirit, decision making process and individual attitudes, and values are some of the barriers of knowledge sharing.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 routine과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: routine = 일상적인, 반복적인
det.analysis:

❌ ③ customary(관례적인)는 routine과 유사한 의미이다
✅ ④ extraordinary(비범한)는 routine(일상적인)의 반의어로, 가장 반대되는 뜻이다 ←정답
det.tip: routine(일상적인) ↔ extraordinary(비범한/특별한). 습관은 routine tasks(일상 업무)에 소비되는 에너지를 줄인다.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 (A)의 밑줄 친 functioned와 (B)의 Functional의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 신체가 얼마나 잘 기능하는지 (B) 부서별 칸막이(조직의 부서 간 장벽)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (B)의 '기능적인(실용적인)'은 Functional silos에서 '기능/부서별 칸막이'라는 의미와 다름. silo는 조직의 부서 간 장벽을 뜻함
✅ ② (A)의 functioned는 '기능하다(작동하다)' = 신체가 얼마나 잘 기능하는지, (B)의 Functional은 '부서별의' = 조직 내 부서별로 나뉜 칸막이(silos)라는 뜻으로 가장 적절 ←정답
❌ ③ (B)의 '기능적인(실용적인)'은 Functional silos 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀌어 있음
det.tip: function: (A) 동사 = 기능하다/작동하다. (B) functional silos = 부서별 칸막이 (조직에서 부서 간 소통 장벽). silo = 원래 '곡물 저장고', 비유적으로 '칸막이'.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the ability to continue a difficult activity for a long period of time without becoming tired"

det.korean: 지치지 않고 오랜 시간 동안 어려운 활동을 계속할 수 있는 능력
det.analysis:
❌ ① efficiency(효율성)는 최소 자원으로 최대 결과를 내는 것으로, 오래 견디는 능력과 다르다
❌ ② intelligence(지능)는 사고/학습 능력으로, 지치지 않고 견디는 능력이 아니다
✅ ③ endurance(지구력)는 '오랜 시간 동안 어려운 활동을 지치지 않고 계속하는 능력'이라는 정의에 정확히 맞는다 ←정답
❌ ④ resistance(저항)는 외부 힘에 대한 저항으로, 활동을 계속하는 능력과 다른 개념이다
det.tip: endurance = endure(견디다) + -ance(~하는 것) = 지구력. 본문의 endurance tests = 지구력 검사.

questions.passage: Clancy and Dollinger found that male students were more likely to submit pictures that captured them engaged in an activity (such as playing a sport), displaying __________ (prize) possessions (such as a car), or alone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 남학생들은 활동에 참여하거나, 소중한 소유물을 보여주거나, 혼자 있는 사진을 제출할 가능성이 더 높았다.
det.analysis: prize(동사: 소중히 여기다)를 과거분사 prized로 바꿔야 한다. 'prized possessions'에서 prized는 과거분사로서 possessions(소유물)를 수식하는 형용사 역할을 한다. '소중히 여겨지는 소유물'이라는 의미.
det.tip: prize(소중히 여기다) → prized(소중한). 과거분사가 명사 앞에서 형용사처럼 쓰이는 구문.

questions.passage: On the one hand, this is efficient: It frees us from having to gather all sorts of new information, from getting sidetracked. Yet on the other hand, because we are __________ (expend) less energy on analyzing what is around us, we may be letting our mental guard down.

det.korean: 반면에 우리 주변을 분석하는 데 에너지를 덜 소비하고 있기 때문에 정신적 경계를 내릴 수 있다.
det.analysis: expend(동사: 소비하다)를 현재분사 expending으로 바꿔야 한다. 'we are expending'에서 are + -ing 형태로 현재진행형을 만든다. because절에서 '에너지를 소비하고 있다'는 진행 중인 상태를 나타낸다.

det.korean: 남성은 자신의 능력과 성취로 자신을 정의하는 경향이 있다.

❌ ④ their academic achievements(학업 성취)는 일부 유사하나 원문은 더 넓은 의미의 abilities and accomplishments이다
det.tip: abilities and accomplishments = 능력과 성취. 여성은 relationships(관계), 남성은 abilities and accomplishments(능력과 성취)로 자신을 정의한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기능적 칸막이, 잘못된 지식 습득 방법, 기술에 대한 지식 부족 등은 지식 공유의 장벽 중 일부이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the advantages of team collaboration(팀 협업의 장점)은 본문이 장점이 아닌 장벽을 나열하는 맥락이므로 부적절
❌ ② the methods of effective communication(효과적 소통 방법)은 본문이 소통 방법이 아닌 공유 장벽을 다루므로 부적절
✅ ③ the barriers of knowledge sharing(지식 공유의 장벽)은 기능적 칸막이, 경쟁 정신 등이 지식 공유를 방해하는 장벽이라는 원문에 정확히 맞는다 ←정답
❌ ④ the principles of organizational success(조직 성공의 원칙)는 본문이 성공 원칙이 아닌 공유 장벽을 다루므로 부적절
det.tip: barriers = 장벽/장애물. 지식을 공유하지 않는 다양한 이유(인정 부재, 시간 부족, 경쟁심 등)가 knowledge sharing의 barriers(장벽)이다.
